title: Are You Smarter Than 96% Of The Population?
summary: Patterns, number rules, word links, codes and spatial traps collide in one fast thinking challenge.

landing.intro: Patterns, codes, word links and logic traps collide in one fast challenge—how many can you solve?

startPrompt.title: Brain Challenge Ready
startPrompt.copy: Watch a short ad to start the test.

about.body:
This fast worldwide puzzle challenge mixes patterns, numerical rules, verbal connections, spatial reasoning, code-breaking, attention and logical deduction in ten varied questions. It is designed to feel playful and surprising rather than like a formal aptitude exam.

Each puzzle has one answer supported by the information shown. The interaction changes regularly, so you may need to spot an alternating symbol, decode a word, reflect an arrow, compare a rule or combine two clues.

Your Smart Score is simply the percentage of these ten entertainment puzzles you solve correctly. It can highlight the kinds of clues that felt most natural in this attempt, but it does not measure intelligence, IQ, aptitude or educational ability.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Solve ten varied thinking challenges at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose one answer per puzzle. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Finish the challenge to unlock your Smart Score and thinking-skill profile.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment only. The Smart Score is a puzzle percentage, not a standardised intelligence, IQ, aptitude or educational assessment.

profiles.title: The Systems Mastermind
profiles.copy: You consistently spotted hidden structure across very different types of problems. Patterns, constraints and small details tended to click into place quickly.

profiles.title: The Precision Thinker
profiles.copy: You combined strong rule detection with careful attention to detail. Even when the format changed, you usually found the important clue.

profiles.title: The Pattern Navigator
profiles.copy: You found your way through most of the vault by recognising how information connected. Your strongest moments came when there was a clear underlying rule to uncover.

profiles.title: The Adaptive Solver
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of challenges and adapted well when the puzzle style changed. Some locks opened instantly; others needed a different angle.

profiles.title: The Curious Analyst
profiles.copy: You cracked a solid share of the vault and kept experimenting when the rule was not immediately obvious. Your result shows a mixed reasoning profile rather than one dominant style.

profiles.title: The Creative Wildcard
profiles.copy: The vault caught you with some of its more structured rules, but you still found solutions across several challenge types. Your answers produced a lively and unpredictable reasoning pattern.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen your puzzle approach
details.tipsIntro: Simple ideas for a future attempt—not an intelligence or aptitude assessment.

tips.title: Name the rule
tips.copy: Before choosing, say the pattern or constraint in a short sentence.

tips.title: Check every clue
tips.copy: In logic puzzles, a small negative or condition often eliminates the tempting answer.

tips.title: Transform one step at a time
tips.copy: For rotations, mirrors and codes, apply each operation separately before comparing choices.

questions.question: Which symbol completes both patterns?

visual.ariaLabel: outline circle, filled triangle, outline square, filled circle, outline triangle, filled square, unknown

questions.explanation: The shapes repeat circle, triangle, square while the fill alternates outline, solid. The next symbol is an outline circle.

questions.question: Use both clues. What is triangle × square?

visual.ariaLabel: two squares equal ten; triangle plus square equals eight

questions.explanation: Two squares total 10, so each square is 5. The triangle is 3, and 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.question: Which word completes both phrases?
questions.explanation: BALL completes both familiar phrases: snowball and ballroom.

questions.question: Which arrow is the reflection in this vertical mirror?

visual.ariaLabel: up-right arrow beside a vertical mirror

questions.explanation: A vertical mirror swaps left and right while preserving height, so an up-right arrow becomes up-left.

questions.question: The shifts repeat +1, +2, +1. How is DOG coded?

visual.ariaLabel: letter shifts repeat plus one, plus two, plus one; CAT becomes DCU

questions.explanation: Apply +1, +2, +1: D becomes E, O becomes Q and G becomes H, producing EQH.

questions.question: Exactly one person tells the truth. A says B lies. B says C lies. C says A and B both lie. Who tells the truth?
questions.explanation: If B tells the truth, C lies. Then A’s claim that B lies is false, and C’s claim that both A and B lie is also false, leaving exactly one truth-teller.

questions.question: Which row breaks the two-part matching pattern?

visual.ariaLabel: Four rows pairing a letter with its successor and a number with its double; the fourth row skips a letter

questions.explanation: Each row should advance the letter by one and double the number. The fourth row doubles 5 correctly but skips from H to J.

questions.question: Apply the same turn: if ↑ becomes ↘, what does ← become?

visual.ariaLabel: An up arrow becomes down-right after the same turn that must be applied to a left arrow

questions.explanation: Up becomes down-right after a 135-degree clockwise turn. Applying that turn to left produces up-right.

questions.question: What comes next?
questions.explanation: After 2, each increase doubles: +1, +2, +4, +8, so the next increase is +16 and 17 + 16 = 33.

questions.question: Four vaults are W, X, Y and Z. It is not W or Z. If it were X, the alarm would be on. The alarm is off. Which vault is it?
questions.explanation: W and Z are ruled out. X would switch the alarm on, but it is off, so Y is the only vault left.
